title: Leading People Who Know More Than You Do or Do Work You’ve Never Done
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The post addresses a problem every rising leader meets: leading experts whose work they have never done and whose questions they cannot answer. The author's answer is that credibility comes neither from pretending to know nor from asking token insightful questions, but from understanding the obstacles that make the experts' work hard, including processes, dependencies, roadblocks and deadlines. What experts want is resourceful support rather than guidance, and they care more that the leader appreciates barriers than that the leader removes them. The author adds that a leader can learn these impediments in weeks, after which they are accepted as an equal partner. The piece gives new leaders of specialist teams a concrete and modest way to earn standing.
points: Leaders of experts earn credibility by understanding the obstacles in the work, not by feigning expertise.
Experts want resourceful support, not guidance or manufactured insightful questions.
Appreciating that a roadblock exists matters more to experts than the leader necessarily removing it.
Learning the impediments takes weeks, not years, and it earns the leader a standing to offer views on the work.
quotes: As a result, leaders are often asked questions they cannot answer or even understand. So, how do leaders show up credibly to those who are more expert than they are?

Learning what makes their work more difficult, the processes and people they depend on to deliver their work, what impediments or roadblocks get in their way, and the deadlines and pressures they face — that’s what experts want from their leaders. They don’t need guidance. They need resourceful support.

Leaders who take the time to understand the hurdles they face gain enormous credibility. Team members don’t expect leaders to remove barriers as much as they desire for those above them to appreciate that the roadblocks exist.

The good news is that observant and inquisitive leaders can learn about impediments in weeks, not months or years. Once armed with this understanding, they are accepted as equal partners in the pursuit of excellence.

While eliminating obstacles and roadblocks is always a blessing, it is understanding what they are that carries the most weight with experts and those who do work leaders are unfamiliar with. Real talent will find a way around or through a roadblock, and they desire a leader who appreciates and assists in the workaround.
